1.plain: All four pots sit under the 80° valve and none moved today: Iran 69° (6.0), US 78° (6.8), Small Gulf 69° (6.0), Saudi–UAE 59° (5.2). The Saudi fall of Friday 03:00 — the Taif death aging out of the seven-day window — is still held for the house's tick, so the day's point is written plain. Inside the numbers: the rial gave back 400 of its Saturday jump (234,800); Brent's weekend close $104.3 stands; no US force was fired on and the only US military aircraft on the feed was a tanker over the Gulf of Oman; Qatar and Pakistan are still carrying messages, so Iran's 'talks' term stays at its lowest setting even with Trump's 'I reject their proposal' on one wire. What would move them: one US force fired on or Brent back over ~$110 for the US pot; one confirmed hit on Saudi or Emirati ground for the Saudi pot — three salvos in three days say the launches will keep coming.
1.trade: Sunday night's open reads three things at once: the president's 'I reject their proposal' (Khaleej Times, first-person, one wire), Tehran's answer that the plan carries the leader's name and the channels stay open, and a fifth day of zero on the AIS export counter while Windward counts 15 million barrels of Sep 23 outflow, two-thirds of it ship-to-ship. That is a floor under Brent, not a spike; the spike needs an act, and there has been none at sea for eighty hours. Polymarket already cut every normalisation leg (traffic normal by Dec 31 20%, no return in 2026 81%). The Sep 24 bond closes (5.18 / 5.47) stand until Monday. The US pot sits two tenths under the valve; the Saudi pot at 5.2 goes straight back over 80° on one confirmed hit.

2.plain: The door closed Thursday at 12 in / 11 out with 76 hulls inside, and by 22:00 UTC Friday had three in and nine out with 71 inside — the in-strait count rose through the evening, the crossings did not. The 24-hour log has an LNG tanker and a bulker out and a bulker, an LPG and a small products tanker in — nothing crude-sized either way — and the export counter sat at 0 bbl all day. Reuters' preliminary count was nine transits on Thursday against a ten-day average of about 18; Al Arabiya's data story says traffic is still below that average. That is the measured door. Against it, a US official now says 40 million barrels moved in 48 hours 'under US escort' — the third telling of Wednesday's sixty ships, still with no CENTCOM release and no AIS echo; PortWatch, stuck at Sep 20, will say.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Fifty items wait for the house's tick and NOTHING new was held at Sep 26 07:00: no act at sea, no fire at US forces, no confirmed hit on Gulf ground, no new valve crossing. The candidate that matters is Trump's 'I reject their proposal' — the first first-person rejection of the seven-day plan, on one wire so far — and the referee cannot score it because the US signal table has no row for a rejection; it is logged as a recheck on the held New York thread (2026-09-24 03:00-4), headlined as a single source and flagged again as a rule gap for Sam to close (is a rejection Squeeze & hold, or Escalate?). The Khatam al-Anbiya warning stands as flagged from 03:00 — a threat, not an act. Pezeshkian's 'coordinated with the leader' and the SNSC's walk-back of the airport threat are statements inside the held thread. The Saudi crossing of Sep 25 03:00 (03:00-1) is still yours; the pot reads 5.2 for a second run. Seven rechecks written; the Oman double-count question stands.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days (Sep 24 freeze, window to Oct 8): Iran seizes or fires on a tanker (41%); a Gulf energy strike is the second card (30%); the Houthis on the Red Sea third (18%); a US warship hit 14%. US: sink more Iranian tankers 53%, bigger escorted convoys 39%, a pause that blesses the corridor 14%. The posteriors have not moved since Sep 11 because every signal since then is held for the house's tick — the 80-country statement, if ticked alone, would move Iran's 'Widen the war' from 1.5% to 2.6% and nothing else. Scorecard after three graded days: Iran's top call has landed three times out of three; the US top call — 'sink more tankers' — has missed twice running (nothing sunk since Sep 8). Brier 0.154.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill, Wednesday close posted Friday: the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47% (Sep 24, FRED) — seven basis points above the Sep 23 closes, which were already the highest since 2007 and 2004; gas $4.478; foreign official custody of Treasuries down $11.4B on the week to $2,597.5B, the third fall in four weeks and about $145B below end-April. Iran's parliament speaker is keeping score in public ('Happy 5.1% 10Y America'). The Senate declined, 49-50, to make the war the president's problem before Nov 3 — so the bill stays his.
7.trade: Bear-steepener with official selling: a custody week of +$30B after an intervention has marked the local top in yields twice (Jul 29, Aug 26) — this week was -$11B, so no top signal. DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: whether a second outlet or a transcript carries Trump's 'I reject their proposal' and whether a formal answer reaches Tehran (Araghchi said none had by noon); Rezaei's ~Sep 27–28 window; whether Qatar or Pakistan produce a dated exchange on the seven-day plan after the rejection, and whether Oman's route thread produces a text; whether the French draft is circulated and what Moscow and Beijing say to it; whether three salvos in three days at the kingdom become a hit (the Saudi pot's 5.2 is one confirmed impact from 80° again); whether the Khatam al-Anbiya warning is followed by anything at a US base or ship (rung 8, strong signal); whether the 80-hour quiet at sea holds through Sunday or UKMTO logs #143; whether the inbound crude tanker on the AIS log loads and leaves; whether the rial's Saturday jump holds; whether FRED's Sep 25 print holds 5.18%; and whether PortWatch's Sep 21–25 prints back the AIS log's zero-barrel days or Windward's 15 million.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
